blocks.text: Omnisient's Server Connect is the automated version of our data anonymisation process which runs behind the Client's firewall. It is a console application written in .NET Core 8.0, which means it is cross-platform compatible.
Server Connect currently supports three data sources: file-based CSV, Parquet, Microsoft SQL Server/Azure SQL, MySQL/MariaDB, and PostgreSQL.

For the file-based data source, a file path directory needs to be specified where the source files must be dropped. Every time the Server Connect application is executed, it will scan the directory for any new files, and it will process the files against the provided configuration.
If the data source is a database, Server Connect will scan a database table, or, using a SQL query, it will check for any new records based on a sequential number or date field within the database.

Multiple configurations can be set up, which allows for the loading of multiple datasets with different schemas. They can even run in parallel, but only one instance per configuration is allowed at a time.

In the Server Connect configuration module, a dataset name, data source details, and the data schema are set up. It also provides for a choice of whether to save the iURNs locally for custom data selections later on or to not save iURNs.
The Server Connect upload process can be run as a once-off command or a scheduler tool can be used to run the application at a scheduled interval period.
Recommended system requirements for Server Connect:

items: Operating system: Windows, Linux, or macOS (supports most modern Windows and Windows Server versions)
RAM: 8 GB or more (depending on the number of parallel uploads)
Disk space: 100 MB for the software; an SSD hard drive is recommended
Other: requires the .NET Core 8.0 SDK (https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/8.0)

blocks.text: These requirements help ensure a smooth experience. Adjust your specifications based on your usage and file sizes.
Installation steps summary
The steps below are required to enable the Server Connect application, and will be described in more detail below:

items: Provision server that you wish to run the application on
Install the .NET Core 8.0 SDK: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/8.0
Download application file from https://api.omnisient.com/downloads/enterprisev2
Unzip downloaded file to a directory on the server
Setup the API Keys in the web application: https://app.omnisient.com
Run Configurator application
The Configurator is a self-hosted web server, which helps you setup configurations for your server
You can either run it directly on a server, but in the case of Linux without any user interface you will need to open port 5000, to access the Configurator screen
Or you can run it on your own machine and copy the configurations to the server
Setup configuration
Make sure data is available as per configuration
Run application with new configuration name
Schedule application to automatically run at specified intervals (optional)

blocks.text: Prerequisites
The server application is compatible with Windows, Linux and Mac OS.
Windows Server specification and requirements

items: Supports most modern Windows + Windows Server versions
RAM: 8GB+ (depending on number of parallel uploads)

blocks.text: Disk space

items: 100MB for software
SSD hard drive is recommended

blocks.text: Make sure you have the .NET Core 8.0 SDK installed. You can download it from: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/8.0
The next step is to set up the server application, either for a Linux or a Windows environment.
Linux version setup
The example below is a bash script that will set up a Server Connect application on Ubuntu 22.04:

# Download the latest packages and install .NET Core 8.0 SDK
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y apt-transport-https sudo wget
wget https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/22.04/packages-microsoft-prod.deb -O packages-microsoft-prod.deb
sudo dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb
sudo apt-get install dotnet-sdk-8.0

# We are going to work in our /opt directory. You can use any directory of your choice
cd /opt

# Downloads latest version
sudo wget https://api.omnisient.com/downloads/enterprisev2
sudo mv enterprisev2 enterprisev2.zip

# Installs Unzip command
sudo apt-get install unzip

# Unzip Server Connect application
sudo unzip enterprisev2.zip -d enterprisev2

# Create savedata directory that will be used to save iURN's
sudo mkdir savedata

# Create uploaded files directory which will be used for your source files.
# This is only applicable if you're using the CSV or PARQUET upload option.
# You can change the directory name to whatever you want.
sudo mkdir uploadedfiles

# Give the user access to write to the directory
sudo chown -R ubuntu:ubuntu /opt/enterprisev2
cd enterprisev2

# Run the Server application with the configuration name as a parameter
sudo dotnet Intersect.Enterprise.Server.v2.dll [Configuration Name]
Run the Configurator on Linux
The example below is a bash script that will run the Configurator on Linux. It is based on the setup above:

# Change to the directory where the Configurator is located
cd /opt/enterprisev2/Config

# Run Configurator
sudo dotnet Intersect.Enterprise.Config.dll
It will start the Configurator and you can access it on http://localhost:5000 or https://localhost:5001.
Make sure the port is open so you can access it. Alternatively, if you can not use that port, you can set up an instance on Nginx or Apache to proxy the website over port 80 or 443.
Windows version setup
You can download the application zip file from https://api.omnisient.com/downloads/enterprisev2 (+- 40MB download size).
Once downloaded, you need to unzip the zip file in its desired application directory.

The first step in setting up the server application is to set up a configuration. You can run the configuration utility by navigating to the Config folder and clicking on the Config/Intersect.Enterprise.Config.exe application. That will start a local web server and you can access the configuration utility by navigating to the local address it provides.

When you launch Server Connect, you choose how to authenticate. There are two options: your username and password, or an API Key and Secret. Pick whichever suits your security requirements and how you use Server Connect.
Username and password
Log in with your Omnisient account credentials.

items: Open Server Connect.
Select Use Username and Password.
Enter your username and password, then click Authenticate. If you have forgotten your password, use the Forgot Password link.
Select your company from the dropdown and click Set Company to continue.

blocks.text: interactive, hands-on use.
API Key and Secret
Authenticate using an API Key (ID) and Secret instead of a username and password. This does not require an interactive login, which makes it the right choice for automated or scheduled uploads.
You need an API Key generated in the platform before you can use this option.

items: Open Server Connect.
Select Use API Key.
Enter your API Key ID and Secret.
Click Authenticate.

blocks.text: automated, or scheduled uploads.

blocks.caption: Authenticating with an API Key and Secret

blocks.text: Tips and best practices

items: Choose the login option that aligns with your security requirements and workflow.
Treat your API Key and Secret as confidential, like a password. Do not share them or store them in plain text.
Use the API Key option for automated workflows and username and password for interactive use.

blocks.text: Troubleshooting
If you have trouble logging in or generating an API Key, contact our support team.
You can set up the configuration details for your server. Currently we support the following data source types:
CSV file type
Most popular delimiters are supported.
Parquet file type
Microsoft/Azure SQL Server, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL
CSV/Parquet data sources
For a CSV/Parquet data source, you need to configure the directory that will contain your CSV/Parquet files and the delimiter.
SQL data sources
For the SQL data sources, you need to provide the credentials by filling out the requested fields or you can enter the connection string in a .NET Core format.
For the SQL data sources, you can provide a database table as a data source or a SQL query. Do not use TOP or LIMIT in your SQL query.

You also need to choose your sequential column, which should be a number or date, so we can load the data in batches. The latest processed value will be saved to the database for when you load new data at a later stage.
The Upload Dataset Name will be your dataset name as seen in the Omnisient Platform.

You need to decide if you want to save the iURNs for later identification. If you choose to save the iURN you need to specify the location where you would like to save the data. Be sure that the location has enough storage space similar in size to your source data.
You need to choose the Data Mapping Schema. You can choose an existing data mapping schema, or you can create a new one by clicking the Add button.

blocks.caption: Selecting or creating a data mapping schema

blocks.text: Depending on if you are uploading from a database or file, you can dynamically add the fields based on your source.
Enter the name for the schema and the notification user who will be emailed if any bad data exists or if your upload has completed.

Click Import to import your fields from your source. If you are using a file to upload, choose the file you wish to upload. For best user experience make sure the file has as few rows as possible, since this process only needs the column headers.
You should also indicate which fields are PII (Personal Identifiable Information) fields and then choose which kind of personal information the field contains.
You also need to specify a location where we can temporarily store the uploaded data, which we download from your data source, then anonymize, then upload to our platform.
The last option is if you would like to receive an email once a batch has been uploaded. This is only recommended if you do once-off uploads or don't upload data too often.
Once you have saved your configuration, you can always return to the configurator to make any changes.
Currently the server is built to run on a scheduled basis. You can use any scheduling tool, or for once-off runs you can just run the command displayed in the information area.

blocks.caption: The run command shown in the information area

blocks.text: [Server Application Path]\Intersect.Enterprise.Server.v2.exe [Your configuration name]
For any further support, please email support@omnisient.com.
The upload process is initiated by the command described in the previous chapter, either typed directly in a command line, or initiated by a script which can be scheduled at regular intervals.

Once initiated, the exact process as with the Omnisient Desktop Connect data onboarding application is executed. All the fields marked as PII (information that can uniquely identify an individual) are tokenised, anonymized and salted before any data leaves the client's server environment. Only anonymized tokens are held on the Omnisient platform and used for analysis and campaigns.

All access to uploaded data is managed by the client. The system is built with privacy-by-design principles and will even detect potential personal information contained in fields not marked as PII by the client.
Anonymisation, tokenisation and upload process

Omnisient is the inventor of the Secure Compounded Matching (SCM) Token process, a hybrid cloud approach using artificial intelligence to solve for issues relating to anonymisation and matching in privacy-by-design platforms. Using SCM, tokens can be matched across any PII field with security features iteratively embedded into the tokens to make them incredibly difficult to break. The technology is future-proofed to accommodate for any new advancements in cryptography.

blocks.text: The data is hashed not only on the client's premises but also once uploaded into the Omnisient cloud, to ensure bad actors cannot re-identify any uploaded, tokenized, and hashed personal data.

chapters.title: Preparing a Dataset for Campaign Activation

blocks.text: If a dataset may be used for campaign activation, it must be marked as Activation Ready during processing in Desktop Connect or Server Connect.
Activation refers to sharing a dataset with an advertising platform (e.g., Meta or TikTok) to create matched audiences for targeted campaigns.
Where to Enable Activation
During dataset configuration in Desktop Connect or Server Connect, locate the Use Dataset for Campaign Activation toggle and enable it before completing processing.

blocks.caption: The Use Dataset for Campaign Activation toggle

blocks.text: Enabling the Activation-ready toggle ensures the dataset is technically prepared for this downstream use.
You should enable Activation if the dataset will be:

items: Used by your organization for targeted advertising campaigns
Shared with a partner who will use the dataset for campaign activation

blocks.text: Important: If Activation is not enabled during processing, the dataset will not be compatible for campaign activation later and will need to be re-uploaded and reprocessed.
Activation Prerequisites
Required Dataset Fields
To prepare a dataset for activation, it must include at least one of the following fields:

items: Email
Phone number

blocks.text: You may include one or both.
Including both Email and Phone is recommended to maximize match rates on activation platforms, but only one is required.
Legal Permission to Use This Data for Advertising
You confirm that:

items: You have a valid lawful basis (including any required consents or permissions) to use the dataset for targeted advertising
Individuals have been appropriately informed
You honor opt-outs and other data subject rights
You are permitted to share the data for audience matching under applicable laws and advertising platform terms

blocks.text: In short: you are legally allowed to use and share this data for campaign activation.
Your Organization Has the Proper Agreement with Omnisient
You confirm that:

items: Your organization has the required agreement(s) in place with Omnisient (e.g., MSA, OPLA, Order Form, and/or DPA)
These agreements authorize the use of the dataset for activation and targeted advertising
This use complies with any contractual restrictions

blocks.text: In short: your organization is contractually authorized to activate this data.
